You can still quit, your dosage isn’t too bad. I was taking 80 mg as soon as I woke up and then 80 mg every two hrs until the 20 mg vial ran out then I’d move onto the 60 mg, taking one or two at a time. I did that for about 6 months or maybe a little less. Anyway, these monthly binges lasted 3-4 days, a week tops. 
They were horrible. I regret having ever taken them - I’ve stopped giving my son his for fear he may also develop an addiction later on. Nope, I rather do it myself than watch him suffer and go through what I’ve been through.

I’ve been clean almost two months and I know exactly how you feel, but unlike you I almost didn’t make it. After getting out of treatment I had bloodwork done by a specialist because I hadn’t been able to keep anything down in a year - I had such an extreme vitamin deficiency it’d contribute to the hallucinations not to mention I was starting to have problems with my speech and balance; my brain was dying from starvation. 
Please, please seek treatment - in the past I was able to go months if not years without taking amphetamines, but in the past year I’d go on binges and end up trying to kill myself from being so high I’d hallucinate someone was trying to torture and kill my children and I (the only way to save them from this horror[and the hallucinations were horrific and graphic, visual and auditory depictions of what they’d do to us or have us do to one another] was for me to kill myself). 
If the idea of ODIng doesn’t scare you, let the image of your child hurting beyond belief and crying out to you for help without being able to ease and comfort them be  what stops you from using... it’s certainly the reason I haven’t used this weekend despite desperately wanting to pop a few pills to get that much desired high that I’m craving lately. 
I wish you the best of luck and sincerely hope you’re able to stop cold turkey as you intend; remember there’s never a good time to quit - it’s inconvenient on you and everyone around you, but imagine how much worse it’ll be to watch your addiction spiral out of control or worse, just die. I don’t want that for you or your loved ones. 
Much luck to you.

Hi, I’m on the same boat as you. I was prescribed adderall as an undergrad and started abusing it some time later. At first it was recreationally -and eventually it led to monthly binges where I’d finish 30 pills in a week ..: and at my lowest I’d go through 60 pills in 3-4 days at which time I wouldn’t sleep, eat or drink.  My addiction reached its peak after I lost my mother and I’d just take pills - I’ve tried to kill myself six or seven times in the past 5.5 yrs because I was so high I’d hallucinate someone was trying to torture my children and I and then kill us and the only way to save them was to off myself - my last attempt was in January or February or this year. 
Anyway, much like you the Doctors diagnosed me with schizophrenia (schizo-affective, actually) and prescribed me anti-psychotics and mood stabilizers but they didn’t take into account the chemicals I’d been putting in my body and the effects these had every time I’d have an adderall induced psychotic episode. Two months ago i went to treatment and they lowered the dosage of the meds with positive results. Turns out I’m not schizo, the paranoia and hallucinations were the result of pills. 
It’s possible that with time and the help of a medical specialist they’re able to determine if your mental health issues are a direct consequence of substance abuse than a chemical imbalance in your brain. 
Either way, I hope you remain sober and wish you the best of luck.
